---
title: "SPEC-4.4.0-v001"
subtitle: "Domain window names on Apply; combine subdomains"
---

## Problems

1. **Default window names after "Apply to Windows".** Applying a
   *Categorize by Website* grouping recycles the existing windows first
   (renaming each to its section's domain) and creates new windows for the
   remaining sections. `tabService.createWindowWithTabs` returned nothing,
   so the new windows could not be named and fell back to the generated
   defaults (`window5`, `window6`, …). With more websites than open windows
   — the usual case — most windows ended up with meaningless names. The
   same gap affected *Categorize with AI*.
2. **Subdomains split a site.** Sections are keyed by full hostname, so
   `account.bambibaby.com` and `www.bambibaby.com` became separate
   sections — and separate windows when applied.

## Changes

### Every applied window is named after its section

- `createWindowWithTabs` now resolves to the new window's id
  (`string | null`; `null` in demo mode or for an empty tab list). Existing
  callers that ignore the result are unaffected.
- `handleApplyAiOrganization` names newly created windows exactly as it
  names recycled ones: the section name (the domain, or the AI category)
  is saved as the window's custom name and added to the name history, so
  name undo/redo covers it.
- **Undo Reorg** also benefits: when a snapshot's window no longer exists
  and is re-created, the re-created window gets the snapshot's name back
  (previously "Name is lost for new ID").
- The website-view confirm message now says windows are "named after its
  domain".

### "Combine subdomains" toggle

UI choice (from four options considered — a toggle in the view, a checkbox
in the Apply confirmation, a second sidebar action, and per-site merge
links): a **checkbox pill in the By Website view's toolbar**, next to
*Sort All*, labelled **Combine subdomains**. Rationale: the sections on
screen always match the windows "Apply to Windows" will create.

- Shown only in the By Website view.
- Toggling regroups the sections immediately; "Close all N", context menus,
  keyboard navigation and Apply all operate on the regrouped sections.
- Persisted in `chrome.storage.local` as `combineSubdomains`
  (default `false`, i.e. existing behaviour).
- When on, sections are keyed by `getSiteOf(hostname)` and titled with the
  site (e.g. `bambibaby.com`); the confirm message says "each site
  (subdomains combined)".

### `getSiteOf` (services/sortUtils.ts)

Maps a hostname to its registrable site:

| Hostname | Site |
|---|---|
| `account.bambibaby.com`, `www.bambibaby.com` | `bambibaby.com` |
| `news.bbc.co.uk` | `bbc.co.uk` |
| `a.b.c.example.org` | `example.org` |
| `localhost`, `local`, `192.168.1.10`, `[::1]` | unchanged |

- Normally keeps the last two labels. If the last two labels form a known
  two-label public suffix (`co.uk`, `com.au`, `co.jp`, … — a built-in list
  of common country-code second levels, not the full Public Suffix List),
  it keeps three.
- IPv4/IPv6 literals and single-label hosts are returned unchanged; a
  trailing dot is ignored.
- Sections are still ordered with `compareDomains`, which already sorts by
  2nd-level label first.

## Docs

- README / in-app User Guide: Combine subdomains and window naming
  described under *Features* and *Categorizing Tabs*.
- Tour step "Categorize by Website" mentions both.

## Version

`package.json` / `manifest.json` bumped **4.3.0 → 4.4.0**.
